Rhinoplasty

Rhinoplasty reshapes the bone and cartilage of the nose to create a nose in balance with your facial features. In many cases it is combined with septal correction to improve breathing in the same operation.

At a glance

Operating time
About 2 to 4 hours
Anaesthesia
General
Hospital stay
Same day or one night
Back to desk work
Typically 10 to 14 days
Book a consultation

Who is it for?

Rhinoplasty may suit people with:

  • a hump on the bridge of the nose
  • a wide, drooping or poorly defined tip
  • asymmetry or deviation, including after injury
  • breathing difficulty associated with the shape of the nose

It is best done once facial growth is complete, from the late teens onward, for people with realistic expectations who want the change for themselves.

How is it done?

There are two main approaches. Open rhinoplasty uses a small incision across the column between the nostrils, which usually heals to a barely visible line. Closed rhinoplasty is performed entirely inside the nostrils, with no external incision. The approach is chosen according to what your nose needs, and preservation techniques are used where suitable.

If the septum is deviated or the turbinates are enlarged, they are treated in the same operation, known as septorhinoplasty.

Recovery

  • First week: an external splint stays on for about a week. Congestion and swelling around the eyes peak in the first two to three days.
  • Two weeks: most visible swelling and bruising has settled, and most patients return to work and social life.
  • 4 to 6 weeks: avoid strenuous exercise and heavy glasses resting on the nose.
  • 12 months or more: residual swelling, especially at the tip, continues to fade until the final shape emerges.

Possible risks

As with any surgery there are risks, which we discuss in detail at consultation. They include bleeding, infection, prolonged swelling, changes in breathing and minor asymmetry. A proportion of patients need a later touch-up procedure. Careful planning and following aftercare instructions reduce these risks but cannot remove them.

Frequently asked questions

Is rhinoplasty painful?

Most patients describe congestion and pressure more than pain, managed with standard pain relief over the first few days.

Will there be a visible scar?

Closed rhinoplasty has no external incision. Open rhinoplasty leaves a small incision under the nose that usually heals to a barely noticeable line.

When will I see the final result?

The general shape is visible within weeks, but the final result typically takes a year or more as swelling resolves, and longer with thick skin.

Can my breathing be improved at the same time?

Yes. A deviated septum or enlarged turbinates can be corrected in the same operation, and breathing is assessed before every aesthetic procedure.

What is the right age for rhinoplasty?

After facial growth is complete, usually from the late teens. There is no fixed upper age limit if your general health is good.

Does the digital simulation mean I'll get exactly that result?

No. The simulation helps us visualise and agree on a goal. The actual result depends on each person's skin, cartilage and healing.
